# Reading policy for the reference kernel (fixed by the orchestrator; every item is reported for arbitration)

General
- The frozen spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md is the only semantic source. Cite clauses as §N or §N.k (item k).
- Formalize each clause as written. Never add a clause the text does not state (no "robustness"); never drop one.
- When a clause has no checkable content in the state (undefined term), do not invent content: omit it from the definition and record it in readings.md (clause, quote, why it cannot be formalized).
- When a clause has two readings, use the one listed below; if the case is not listed, use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings, and record it in readings.md with both readings and an example of a program whose verdict changes.
- A representation choice that changes no accepted program is free (record it briefly).

State (§38): S3 = (F, nF, P, I, A, D, dead, pin). No arena registry, no callParams, no freed. Library state lives elsewhere.
Outcomes (§58): one type Outcome3 σ := ok σ | reject | fail; every O1–O16 relation except alloc never yields fail.
O1 derive (§60): takes a region (List Nat, read extensionally), not a place. Preconditions: active source; ExercisableAt source mode; every leaf of region exists, is a leaf, belongs to afp source; mode ≤ effective mode of source on each leaf; §60.3 as a decidable clause (no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible); §60.4 current frame live. §60.1c "origin chain and anchors valid" and §60.4b "footprint and anchoring restrictions": no checkable content -> omitted, recorded.
O2 split (§61): draft clauses (incl. no exclusive right already distributed). §61.4 is NOT a precondition (the §61 note says an accepted split may violate I1 without DDSound) -> recorded.
O3 release (§62): draft clauses; §62.5 (abstraction contracts) omitted, recorded.
O4 transfer (§63): draft clauses MINUS the draft's extra clause "(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst" (not in §63); PLUS §63.8 (local self-blocking prevention, as LockOptions.Opt2Transfer on formal/derivability_0.1); effect: dependencies follow the corresponding places corr(r) (not all to the destination root); §63.6 over moved usable places and AnchorOrder in the resulting state; §63.7 AnchorOrderHeld for the moved held authorities in the resulting state; §63.4 = draft ActiveDerivedOutside reading (recorded); §63.2 child order = place index order (recorded).
O5 depend (§64): draft clauses; §64.2b "real dependency" omitted, recorded.
O8 store (§65): draft clauses (they match).
O9/O10/O11 (§66–§68): add "every leaf belongs to a usable place" (§66.1, §67.1, §68.1); O10 keeps §67.2 explicitly.
O12 endUse (§69): death markers transitive over owned storage; drop the draft's extra disjunct that blocks descendants of authorities the step releases (not in §69.2) -> record the consequence.
O13 free (§70): death markers transitive; no extra "Usable p" and no clearing of D beyond what §70 prescribes; §70.4 scope = the released unit (place and storage that dies with it).
O14 alloc (§71): shape nonempty with exactly ONE root (one new storage root), parts' parents inside the shape, no owner component; provider clause as written in §71.2 (Modify OR writeShared over SharedMutable metadata) -> conflict with §36 recorded; outcomes reject / fail (not Satisfiable) / ok.
O6 enterFrame (§72): locals owned directly by the new frame (no local owned by another local); §72.3 ParamOriginHidden; §72.4 AnchorOrderHeld in the resulting state.
O7 exitFrame (§73): draft (first surviving active origin, held by a frame or a usable place).
O15/O16 pin/unpin (§74, §75): per-leaf dynamic pin flags (draft); unpin requires the place usable and K.ExternalDone(place) on the place; StaticPinnedBottom is a condition on (K, statics), not on states.
HasRight / ExercisableAt (§43): one authority exercisable at m with sufficient effective mode on every leaf (∃ a, ∀ l) as the draft -> recorded.
WF3 (§49): a structure with eight named fields, one per item:
 1 frames: F nonempty, no duplicates, every frame < nF;
 2 places: parent links valid and acyclic (representation: parent index < child index), parts share the owner and death marker of their parent;
 3 owners: owner frames < nF, owner places exist; "well-founded ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place" read as stated for usable places (Usable is inductive) -> recorded with the global-acyclicity alternative;
 4 footprints: every footprint member is an existing leaf;
 5 authorities: origins exist and precede (origin index < id: representation of acyclic chains ending at a root);
 6 RootChain (draft);
 7 RootHeld as §49.7 states it: every usable root place has an active root authority, Modify, no origin, held by its owner, whose footprint is the place's footprint (draft RootLive + mode);
 8 holder validity (draft poss).
 The draft's converse RootHeld (every origin-less authority covering a leaf of root r is held by r's owner) is NOT a WF3 clause: keep it as a separate auxiliary predicate.
I2 (§51): mode conservation unconditional (not under ∀ p ∈ footprint).
Initial state (§47): base frame 0; statics may be owned by statics; root authority held by the owner. Well-formedness of the statics declaration (acyclic ownership, parents before children) is not stated by §47: keep the draft ShapeOK-style hypothesis as a hypothesis of the init theorems and record it as a spec gap.
Reachable: closure of S3.init statics under the kernel steps O1–O16 only.
# Reference formalization pass log (ub-mode)
1. Read spec v0 in full, Charter-level files, AGENTS, CLAUDE, DESIGN — CLAUDE.md requires reading the covered passages first.
2. Step 0: copied spec verbatim, sha256 65f9f91f… identical, committed 999bdc5 `docs(specs): add ERN Memory Model Specification v0`, pushed to main (accepted; remote printed a PR-rule notice), verified remote blob checksum.

New findings: P-T2 §63.7 only checks moved authorities (AnchorOrderHeld gap, unreachable witness, HeldAnchored conjecture); §78.3 remark false; §86 contradicted (reissued block reads former value); refinement zero-size non-empty region pointer undecided (PtrDecided hypothesis); pinned leaf unusable after cycle transfer. Committed af4979e..e3b425c (8 commits).

# Report — arena (spec v0 Part XIV, §76–§78, with §36, §46, §55, §56, §58, §79, §86, §88)

File: `formal/Ern/MemoryModel/Arena.lean` (new, untracked; module `Ern.MemoryModel.Arena`,
namespace `Ern.MemoryModel.Arena`, imports `Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Preserve.Common` only).
Nothing committed. No other file touched.

## Status

- `lake build Ern.MemoryModel.Arena`: success, no warnings (`lake env lean` prints nothing).
- `axcheck.sh Ern.MemoryModel.Arena`: 485 constants, 202 theorems, `outside propext, Quot.sound: #[]`
  (no `Classical.choice`).

- Every declaration (196 top-level) has an English docstring citing a § clause (checked by script); no

## Definitions (clause → Lean)

- §46: `ArenaEntry {storage, internal, available, issued}`; `LState = ⟨kern : S3, arenas⟩` (registry
  separate from `S3`); `LState.init` (§47, empty registry); `Live` (internal active); `arenaValue`;
  `Avail` (leaf-wise, empty region available).
- §36/§77.1/§78.1: `MetaRight s E := OptP (arenaValue s E) (HasRight s .modify ·) False` (no

- §55: `ArenaInv` (structure, 9 fields: storage usable; `afp internal = footprint storage`; internal
  active; own mode Modify and held by a place; available ⊆ storage; issued ⊆ storage; two active

- §56/§76.4: `Guard56 (regs : List (List Nat)) i := ∀ R ∈ regs, i ∉ R` — the guard as a contract
  predicate over ALL registries of live administrations (each registry = its live `internal` ids);
  the arena registry contributes `liveInternals s arenas`, the others are the parameter `others`.
- O17 §76: `NewArenaBase` (fields §76.1 ×2, §76.2 ×2, §76.3 ×3, §76.5), `NewArenaPre = base ∧ guard
  (liveInternals :: others)`, `newArenaEff` (appends `⟨st, i, footprint st, []⟩`, kernel unchanged),
  `NewArenaStep others` = `Guarded`.
- O18 §77 contract: `IssueStatic` (§77.1 ×2, §77.2 ×6), `IssueRight` (§77.5), `issueKEff` (block `|A|`

  presents the recorded token). Consequence: every root is deallocatable (`deallocable_sound`);
  `K.Deallocable` is not otherwise used.
- `exitFrame` deallocates the allocations of root places directly owned by the exiting frame and
  not marked dead (`exitRoots`); storage they own leaks (§73 "does not entail automatic physical
  deallocation of all dead places"). Whether automatic storage must be deallocated is not fixed by

Un cas sans source qui tranche est marqué « à arbitrer »." For the reference, the sources MM-02 v0.4 / MM-03.3 v0.3 are superseded by spec v0; expected verdicts must be re-derived from spec v0 clauses (column "spec v0" below), and every change against the material verdict is reported, not applied silently (rule 4).

23	- **Rule 3, reached states.** "Chaque cas est construit depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés."
24	- **Rule 4.** "Pas de correction silencieuse. Un verdict obtenu différent de l'attendu est rapporté avec l'état et le pas en cause."
25	- **Rule 5, class.** "**Classement.** Chaque cas relève de : noyau MM-03 (`N3`), machine MM-02 (`N2`), raffinement (`R`), instance de bibliothèque (`Lib` : arène, pool), ou d'une autre spécification (spec 2, 3, 4, 11). Les cas d'une autre spécification restent des obligations inter-spécifications ; ils ne bloquent pas la clôture du jalon 3." MM2-H and MM23-H tables have no class column (MM2-H is N2 by construction; MM23-H is R; J3 assigned H14 → spec 3, H17 → spec 4/11). W1–W3 are not classed by the material (J3 (f) 17 chose Lib).

# ERN — Jalon 3 : matériel pour revue unique

**Objet :** validation adversariale du Memory Model (spec 1) après les jalons 1 et 2.
**Contenu :** les trois corpus mis à jour, le contrat du pool de handles, le cadrage de la décision `NoLock`, le registre des obligations inter-spécifications.
**Statut :** matériel de conception, non normatif. Version 2 : corrections de la revue unique de GPT intégrées (contrat du pool, corpus, calendrier, scénarios Weld).

## 0. Règles du jalon 3

1. **Oracle indépendant.** Le verdict attendu d'un cas vient de sa source (clause de MM-02 v0.4, de MM-03.3 v0.3, arbitrage, ou usage déclaré), jamais du comportement des modules. Un cas sans source qui tranche est marqué « à arbitrer ».
2. **Jumeau positif.** Chaque rejet a un jumeau minimal accepté : même séquence sans l'élément fautif. Un rejet qui persiste dans le jumeau est un défaut de construction.
3. **États atteints.** Chaque cas est construit depuis l'état initial par des pas autorisés.
4. **Pas de correction silencieuse.** Un verdict obtenu différent de l'attendu est rapporté avec l'état et le pas en cause.
5. **Classement.** Chaque cas relève de : noyau MM-03 (`N3`), machine MM-02 (`N2`), raffinement (`R`), instance de bibliothèque (`Lib` : arène, pool), ou d'une autre spécification (spec 2, 3, 4, 11). Les cas d'une autre spécification restent des obligations inter-spécifications ; ils ne bloquent pas la clôture du jalon 3.
6. **Couverture.** La colonne « Couvert » indique un témoin déjà produit pendant les jalons 1 et 2, quand il est identifié avec certitude. Le jalon 3 rejoue tous les cas depuis l'état initial, couverts ou non, dans un module de cas séparé.
7. **Cible des corpus.** MM3-H et MM23-H sont encodés au jalon 3 sur les brouillons, sans modifier `MM02`, `MM03` ni `MM23`. MM2-H : ses verdicts sont révisés au jalon 3, mais sa validation exécutable reste une obligation de la reconstruction de référence ; le jalon 3 ne le déclare pas validé.
8. **Écarts connus.** Un cas dont le verdict attendu repose sur une décision non encore appliquée au brouillon (MM23-H15, H16) est encodé avec le verdict obtenu, marqué « écart connu », et inscrit au registre de reconstruction. Il n'est jamais présenté comme réussi.

---

| H50 | Autorité transférée ou émise dans l'emplacement qu'elle couvre | à arbitrer (§5) | N3, Lib | passe 7 (`held_unexercisable_by_*`) |
| H51 | Élément d'un stockage possédé par `v` qui range une vue sur `v` | à arbitrer (§5) | N3 | — |

### J. Hors noyau (obligations inter-spécifications)

| ID | Scénario | Attendu | Spécification |
|---|---|---|---|
| H38 | Cache *get-or-insert* : accès à l'entrée trouvée, ou insertion puis accès | `ok` | spec 3 (vivacité sensible au flot) |
| H39 | Coroutine suspendue tenant un paramètre `Modify` pendant que l'appelant reprend | l'appelant ne touche pas l'empreinte tant que la coroutine détient l'autorité | specs 2, 3 |
| H40 | Pointeur brut obtenu avant un appel, utilisé pendant l'appel sur l'empreinte d'un paramètre `Modify` | UB | MM-02.G, spec 3 |
| H41 | `writeShared` concurrent | sûr seulement sous contrat synchronisé | spec 2 |
| H42 | `defer free(x)` puis `transfer(x)` avant une sortie | `reject` | spec 3 |
| H43 | Ressource à obligation (fichier) ouverte puis abandonnée | `reject` si le type porte l'obligation | spécification des ressources |

---

## 5. Décision `NoLock` — cadrage

**Fait établi (passe 7).** Des états atteints contiennent des autorités détenues que personne ne peut exercer, ce qui bloque un `reset` ou un `free` jusqu'à la mort d'une ressource englobante (H49–H51). Ces états respectent tous les invariants de sûreté ; la charte exclut les interblocages du contrat de sûreté (§4.1). C'est une question d'ergonomie et de progrès, pas de sûreté.

**Options**

1. **Aucune règle** (référence de comparaison). Les blocages sont admis ; les relations persistantes passent par des handles par convention.
2. **Règle locale.** Interdire qu'une opération place une autorité dans un emplacement qu'elle couvre (auto-blocage). O8 l'interdit déjà pour `store` ; le gain à mesurer porte sur `transfer` et `issue`. Ne couvre pas les cycles de longueur ≥ 2 construits par autorité auxiliaire.
3. **`NoLock` global.** Acyclicité de la relation « `b` bloque `a` », auto-blocage défini comme clause séparée, vérifiée à l'arrivée de `transfer`, `issue`, `store`.

**Mesures à produire au jalon 3, pour chaque option :**
- faux rejets sur les cas qui doivent être acceptés : H11, H19, H29b, H35–H37, H44–H47, W1–W3 ;
- blocages résiduels sur H49–H51 ;
- coût d'analyse : la vérification est-elle locale à une fonction, ou exige-t-elle une analyse globale ?

**Critère de choix** : aucune option n'est adoptée si elle rejette un cas qui doit être accepté. Entre options sans faux rejet, la moins coûteuse à analyser l'emporte.

---

## 5b. Scénarios d'usage (exigences de validation, pas une description de l'implémentation actuelle de Weld)

| ID | Structure | Séquence | Attendu |
|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | Graphe de scène | Pool de nœuds `{data, parent : handle, child : handle}` sur une allocation ; deux nœuds liés dans les deux sens par handles ; `resolve` `Modify` d'un nœud, écriture de `data`, `unresolve` ; `freeSlot` d'un nœud encore désigné par le handle de l'autre ; `resolve` de ce handle ; `freeSlot` pendant une résolution active | tout `ok` ; `resolve` du handle périmé : `fail` ; `freeSlot` pendant résolution : `reject` |
| W2 | ECS archetype + sparse set | Archetype à deux colonnes (SoA) sur une allocation ; `split` des colonnes ; système A écrit la colonne 1 pendant que le système B lit la colonne 2 ; `resolveMany` `Modify` de trois entités distinctes d'un pool d'entités ; déplacement d'une entité vers un autre archetype (transferts des champs de la ligne) pendant qu'une vue de colonne est active, puis après sa libération | lectures et écritures disjointes `ok` ; `resolveMany` `ok` ; déplacement pendant la vue : `reject` ; après : `ok` |
| W3 | Arène de frame | `alloc`, `newArena`, trois `issue`, trois vues rangées (`store`) dans une structure locale ; `reset` pendant que les vues vivent ; `endUse` de la structure ; `reset` ; réémission | `reset` pendant : `reject` ; après : `ok` ; réémission `ok` |

## 6. Registre des obligations inter-spécifications

| Obligation | Destination |
|---|---|
| `stat` (composante concurrente des obligations opaques) ; transférabilité, partageabilité ; H39, H41 | spec 2 |
| Protection forte des paramètres (`Reach`, `lineage`, `derivedIn`, G1', A3 strict) ; H27b ; H38, H40, H42 ; `defer` | spec 3 |
| `dec` (validité de représentation) ; `SameSizeAlong` ; une référence se range dans un emplacement de type référence ; `kind` comme point d'accroche ; le type d'un pointeur porte la forme d'une région non contiguë (le pointeur n'en désigne que l'adresse la plus basse) | spec 4 |
| `dec` (alignement des accès) ; taille d'un pointeur et encodage `decode` ; largeur des adresses et épuisement de l'espace ; débordement des générations ; placement (`PlacementOK`), jetons (`TokCompat`) | spec 11 |
| Traduction bas niveau de `noalias` | spec 13 |
| Obligation de libération attachée à certains types ; H43 | spécification des ressources |
| `DeclaredDisjoint` (disjonction des feuilles déclarées) ; `FreeCompat` ; représentation des métadonnées d'arène et de pool | bibliothèque |

## 7. Registre de la reconstruction de référence

0. Exécution de MM2-H (17 cas) contre la reconstruction de MM-02 ; MM23-H15 et H16 rejoués après application des décisions 2 et 3 du jalon 2.
1. Écarts du brouillon MM-03 trouvés au jalon 2 (passe 1, (f) 1–6) : utilisabilité des feuilles lues et écrites ; empreintes faites de feuilles ; une racine par `alloc` ; marques de mort transitives ; `RootLive` ; bonne fondation des chaînes de possession.
2. Locaux d'`enterFrame` possédés directement par le cadre (O6, à écrire dans la v0.3).
3. Décisions 1 à 4 du jalon 2 : disjonction déclarée par feuilles ; pointeur d'une région vide ; adresse la plus basse ; feuille de référence de la taille d'un pointeur.
4. Théorèmes à énoncer : induction « toute feuille `Init` atteinte a été déclarée ou écrite » ; correspondance `Step` ↔ `Reachable`.
5. Noms Lean des textes normatifs déplacés en annexe de correspondance.

# VI. Abstract Authority Machine

The components described below constitute the logical state of the sequential discipline. They prescribe neither generalized runtime metadata nor reference syntax.

## 38. Machine State

The access discipline is based on the finite state

\[ S_3=(F,P,I,A,D) \]

where `F` represents the frame stack, `P` the places, `I` their initialization, `A` the authorities, and `D` the validity anchors. Administrative states of arenas and other library abstractions are separate from `S₃`. The external contract `K` is a separate parameter. The internal representation may carry auxiliary information that creates no new rights.

## 39. Execution Frames

`F` is a nonempty stack of identified, non-duplicate frames. Every frame except the initial frame knows its parent. Frames hold temporary authorities and directly local places. The **current frame** is at the top of the stack. `ancestor(f₁, f₂)` means `f₁` is `f₂` or an ancestor of `f₂` in the stack and its call chain.

The base frame, whose identity is 0 in states reachable from the initial state, never exits. An exited frame can neither be the terminal owner of a usable place nor hold an authority that remains active. Frames have semantic existence; no particular runtime representation is required.

## 40. Logical Places, Leaves, and Ownership

A place has an identity, optionally a structural parent, an abstract `kind`, an owner `owner : Frame | Place`, and a logical death marker. Structural parenthood `partOf(p,q)` describes the subplaces of a value; `owner` describes **who keeps the storage** of a root place valid. An owned place may lie outside its owner's direct footprint; ownership and composition are therefore distinct.

A **leaf** is a place with no structural children. `footprint(p)` contains the leaves of `p`, and access rights over a place are evaluated on those leaves. Places transitively owned by a value are not automatically leaves of its `footprint`. A logical unit of the access discipline does not automatically constitute an additional allocation in the elementary memory machine.

A place `p` is **usable** (`Usable(s,p)`) if and only if:

1. `p` exists and is not marked dead;
2. if its owner is a frame, that frame belongs to the stack;
3. if its owner is a place `q`, then `q` is itself usable and the chain terminates at a frame in the stack.

An ownership cycle makes no place usable. `placeFrame(p)` is the terminal frame of this chain when `p` is usable. Structural parts share their parent's owner and death marker. A value may be logically ended by `endUse` without the place that contained it becoming unusable; the substorages it owned may, however, die.

A **root place** has no structural parent. Every root place has a root authority of own mode `Modify`, with no origin, held exactly by that place's owner (`RootHeld`). This authority cannot be transferred in isolation; root ownership follows a legal transfer of the owning value when necessary.

## 41. Leaf Initialization States

Every tracked leaf has exactly one of the states `Uninit`, `Init`, or `Moved`.

- `Uninit`: no initialized value available in this leaf.
- `Init`: initialized value, subject to type, representation, and storage obligations.
- `Moved`: value consumed by transfer, inaccessible as its former value.

Aggregates may be partially initialized. Both `Uninit` and `Moved` prohibit ordinary reads, while remaining distinct states for diagnostics and end-of-use obligations. An initialization state creates no access permission.

## 42. Authorities, Modes, Holders, and Origins

An authority conceptually has the following fields:

```text
Authority {
    id
    mode: Observe | Modify
    origin?: AuthorityId
    footprint: Set<Leaf>
    holder: Frame | Place
    active: Bool
}
```

`origin` links a derived authority to its current origin. Authorities have fresh identities and well-formed origin chains. A root authority has no origin; a derived authority has one. Creating derived rights does not increase the scope or permitted mode of the origin.

The **holder** (`holder`) is not the **owner** (`owner`). An authority derived by `derive` or `split` is initially held by the current frame; `store` or a permitted transfer may make it held by a place. The derived `issue` operation proceeds through `split` followed by `store`. `release` does not release a root. There is no persistent `Suspended` field: suspension of rights is inferred from active descendants and applies leaf by leaf.

## 43. Effective Rights and Exercise of Authorities

For an authority `a` and a leaf `l`, `effective(s,a,l)` is derived from the active descendants of `a` whose footprint contains `l`:

1. if `a` is inactive or does not cover `l`, its effective mode is absent;
2. if no active descendant covers `l`, the effective mode is the own mode of `a`;
3. if an active descendant with own mode `Modify` covers `l`, the effective mode of `a` is absent;
4. otherwise, when the covering active descendants are `Observe`, the effective mode of `a` on `l` is `Observe`.

The effect is **local to each leaf**: after splitting a region, the origin may retain effective `Modify` over undistributed leaves.

Requested modes are ordered `Observe ≤ Modify`. `ExercisableAt(s,a,m)` means:

- `a` is active and its own mode permits `m`;
- either `a` is held by the current frame;
- or `a` is held by a place `p`, and the current frame has, over **all** leaves of `p`, an authority itself exercisable in mode `m` with sufficient effective mode.

The latter clause is recursive along the holder chain. Thus, being active or covering a leaf does not automatically make an authority exercisable. `HasRight(s,m,p)` means the current frame has exercise in mode `m` and sufficient effective mode **over every leaf in `p`'s footprint**. Every operation requires the modes it actually needs; an authority's own mode alone is insufficient.

## 44. Dependencies and Effective Anchors

`D(p)` is the set of authorities serving as **validity anchors** for place `p`. An anchor is valid as long as the authority it names is active. Dependencies of contained values are accounted for transitively. Relevant dependencies follow the value during transfer; those of its container do not automatically follow a part transferred in isolation.

For an authority `x`, its **effective anchor** is the root reached by traversing its origin chain. It does not necessarily coincide with its current holder. Lifetime constraints are calculated from the frame of that effective anchor and the frames of places that remain usable. A dependency cannot create a right or artificially extend a lifetime.

`AnchorOrder` requires, for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, that the frame of the effective anchor of `x` be the frame of `q` or one of its ancestors. `AnchorOrderHeld` imposes the same rule on every **active authority held** by `q`. These conditions apply to the resulting states of operations that move or create holder relations.

## 45. Parameters, Returns, and Reanchoring

A call parameter is an **active derived authority held by the caller** before being passed to the callee; its original provenance may go back to an earlier frame. This interpretation does not require that the authority was originally derived in the calling frame; that additional requirement belongs to Spec 3. The caller **yields** the authority to the new frame: it does not simultaneously retain a copy. If the authority remains in that frame upon return, `exitFrame` releases it; **it is not automatically returned to the caller**. To retain its own right, the caller may pass a **fresh derivative** of the authority it wishes to keep: this is ordinary reborrowing. The definition of ergonomic calling conventions is deferred to Spec 3.

A result is returned by a legal `transfer` into the result place provided by the caller as a `Modify` parameter. Surviving authorities and their dependencies are reanchored by `exitFrame` to still-valid origins. There is no standalone correspondence `M` and no implicit escape permission.

## 46. Arenas as Library Administration States

Each entry belongs to the library's abstract state, **separate from kernel state `S₃`**. It has the following fields:

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Leaf>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

A region is **available if and only if each of its leaves belongs to `available`**; the empty region is always available. Issuance removes the leaves of the issued region from `available`. Reset restores all leaves of the administered storage to that set. The registry and its updates belong to the abstraction contract and create no kernel permissions.

The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.

## 47. Initial State

The kernel's initial state contains only base frame 0 and the declared static storage. Every static leaf has its declared initial state, `Init` or `Uninit`. The roots of static places directly owned by frame 0 have a root `Modify` authority held by that frame; a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter. The initial state invents no dynamic allocation, derived authority, or implicit anchor. The initial arena registry belongs to library state and is empty. The initial frame does not exit.

## 48. External Parametric Contract

`K` contains the predicates `DeclaredDisjoint`, `SharedMutable`, `Pinned`, `ExternalDone`, `Deallocable`, `FreeCompat`, and `Satisfiable`. Their obligations are specified in Section 80. `K` can neither fabricate access rights nor remove an obligation of the Charter. The predicate `Invalidates` is not part of this contract.

# VII. Invariants of Reachable States

Machine states are subject to structural, validity, and exclusivity requirements preserved by permitted transitions under their declared external contracts.

## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
4. footprints consisting exclusively of leaves of existing places;
5. authorities with valid identities and modes, whose existing origins form **acyclic** chains ending at a root authority;
6. `RootChain`: every origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root of the **same structural root place** as that leaf;
7. `RootHeld`: every usable root place has its active root `Modify` authority, with no origin, held exactly by its owner;
8. holder validity: every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place.

Numerical ordering of identifiers, parent precedence over child in a list, and bounds on generated identifiers may be used **to represent or prove** this well-formedness in a formalization; they are not normative restrictions on place or authority identities. Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a **required property of transitions**, not an additional clause of the state predicate. `WF3` does not impose any particular physical object layout: that belongs to refinement into the elementary memory machine.

## 50. I1 — Structural Exclusivity

For two active authorities **unrelated by derivation** covering the same leaf, their own modes must both be `Observe`. This rule also applies to leaves identified as `SharedMutable`; their particular mutation is governed by the `writeShared` contract and creates no exception to I1.

Exclusivity of **effective** modes (`effective_exclusive`) is a consequence of I1 and the definition of `effective`, not the definition of I1. On a leaf, two incompatible authorities cannot simultaneously possess incompatible effective rights. The only permitted independent ordinary coexistence is `Observe` / `Observe`.

## 51. I2 — Conservation of Rights

A derived authority covers only a subfootprint of what its origin chain permits and does not elevate its mode. Derivation and splitting restrictions do not allow duplication of an exclusive right over a leaf. Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules. Partial suspension follows from `effective`.

## 52. I3 — Validity of Anchors and Dependencies

Every explicit anchor of a still-usable place is valid. An operation cannot invalidate an anchor retained by a place that remains usable. Transitive propagation of dependencies from contained values does not change this obligation. Dependencies are not permissions and are insufficient to justify an access.

## 53. I4 — Consumption and Movement

A `Moved` leaf cannot be read as if it still contained its previous value. Moving a value does not preserve two copies of an exclusive authority. Initialization state and authority-exercise state are separate checks.

## 54. Anchor Ordering and Absence of Orphan Rights

`AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` are defined in Section 44. `NoDangling` prohibits an **active** authority from covering a leaf belonging to an unusable place; the invariant does not say that a leaf is initialized. `NoOrphan` requires every active authority held by a place to be connected to a frame in the stack through a **finite, non-repeating chain** of authorities: the first link is held by a live frame, and each active link **structurally covers the entirety** of the place holding the next link. The link need not have an effective mode over that place. `NoOrphan` guarantees neither the exercisability of all stored authorities nor freedom from blocking.

## 55. ArenaInv — Invariant of the Arena Abstraction

`ArenaInv` is an invariant of the **library contract**, not an additional predicate of kernel state. For every live arena:

- `storage` designates an existing, usable place; the footprint of `internal` is exactly the footprint of `storage`;
- `internal` is active, with own mode `Modify`, held by the arena value;
- available leaves and issued regions belong to the administered storage;
- two still-active issuances have disjoint regions; no leaf of a still-issued region simultaneously belongs to `available`;
- every still-issued block authority is a derivative of `internal` complying with exclusivity and validity rules;
- anchor and ownership restrictions are respected.

Arena entries do not, by themselves, constitute an additional storage owner. Two live arenas may cover common leaves when their `internal` authorities are distinct and their effective rights are compatible; no **global** disjointness of arena footprints is imposed.

## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

I5, associated with pinned storage, remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone. This property is required for reachable states under the declared assumptions. Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below.

# VIII. Definition of Transitions and Management of Authorities

The following operations are abstract transition rules. They distinguish rejection by the discipline, defined failure, and a permitted transition.

## 58. Transition Outcomes

Every operation has a conceptual outcome among:

```text
Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail
```

`reject` means that the static discipline does not permit the step; it is neither an implicit runtime trap nor `ub` in the elementary memory machine. `fail` is a **defined failure** leaving the state unchanged; **only `alloc` may produce it in the O1–O16 kernel**. Other kernel operations produce `ok` or `reject`. Library-abstraction operations, including `issue` (§77), may define their own `fail` cases. Where such failure is provided, static preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract.

An `ok` transition must satisfy its preconditions, apply exactly its prescribed effects, and preserve the relevant invariants. No transition fabricates a permission to make its conclusion true. Holder and anchor changes are evaluated in the **resulting state** when a rule explicitly so provides.

## 59. Implicit Preservation of Modes and Anchors

Changes in effective authority are **derived** from active authorities and their origins; no `Suspended` indicator is mutated. Access operations do not change an anchor without an explicitly authorized effect of transfer, `depend`, `store`, release, or reanchoring. Leaves becoming `Init` do so through a permitted write (`write3`, `writeShared`, `store`, including during a derived `issue`) or a transfer from a corresponding source leaf already `Init`; leaves initialized in `S3.init` are declared as such.

## 60. O1 — Derivation of an Authority

**Preconditions**

1. `source` is an active derived or root authority, and `ExercisableAt(s,source,mode)` holds; its origin chain and anchors are valid.
2. The leaves of `region` exist and belong to the footprint of `source`; `mode` does not exceed the available effective right on these leaves.
3. The addition preserves exclusivity I1: no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible with the derived right, and already-active descendants are respected.
4. The new holding frame is the live current frame. The admissible state's footprint and anchoring restrictions remain true.

**`ok` effect:** A new active authority with fresh identity, origin `source`, requested mode and footprint, and held by the current frame is added. The source remains active; its effective modes are recomputed per leaf. No storage or place anchor is created. Multiple compatible observations remain permitted. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 61. O2 — Splitting Authorities

**Preconditions**

1. `source` is active and exercisable by the current frame with sufficient modification rights over the relevant leaves.
2. Each region lies within the available, effectively modifiable footprint of the source.
3. Regions are pairwise disjoint under structural composition or contract `K.DeclaredDisjoint`, subject to obligation `DDSound(K)`; no exclusive right already distributed is overlapped.
4. Creation of the derivatives respects origins, conservation I1/I2, and validity obligations.

**`ok` effect:** An active derived `Modify` authority held by the current frame is created for each region. `source` remains active; its effective modification capability disappears only over distributed leaves and remains on undistributed leaves. Authorities are split logically: `split` performs no physical allocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

An unjustified declaration of disjointness may invalidate the proof: without `DDSound`, an accepted `split` may violate I1. Constructing zero-sized subregions is not identified with an allocation of the elementary memory machine; the case of an empty shape in `alloc` is distinct.

## 62. O3 — End of a Derived Borrow

**Preconditions**

1. `authority` is active **and derived**: an authority with no origin is rejected.
2. It is held by the current frame, or by a place `p` on which the current frame has exercisable `Modify`.
3. No active descendant of the authority prevents its release; no other still-usable value may lose a required anchor.
4. If the authority is stored in its holding place, that place is exempted from the check “this authority still appears among the anchors” **only because the effect removes that anchor at the same time**. An anchor with the same identity attached by `depend` to another usable place continues to block the step.
5. Applicable abstraction contracts remain satisfied.

**`ok` effect:** The authority becomes inactive and can no longer be exercised. It is removed from its holding place's anchors when stored there. Effective modes of its origins are recomputed, allowing unblocked rights to return. There is no implicit deallocation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

3	# IX. Transfer, Dependencies, and Storage of Rights
4	
5	These transitions govern value consumption and the controlled movement of their dependencies. A valid transition can neither create an additional permission nor discard a surviving anchor.
6	
7	## 63. O4 — Consuming Value Transfer
8	
9	**Preconditions**
10	
11	1. `source` and `destination` are usable, and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over their relevant footprints.
12	2. Source and destination have the **same shape of ordered subtrees**. The `i`-th child of each source part corresponds to the `i`-th child of the corresponding destination part; all nodes are matched. Structural field identity is positional, not an arbitrary matching of children.
13	3. **All** source leaves are `Init`, and **no** destination leaf is `Init`. The source and destination footprints are disjoint.
14	4. No exclusive authority is duplicated; validity of derived authorities and active projections is preserved.
15	5. **No in-place source leaf is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). Storage merely **owned** by the source, which is not itself moved by the transfer of that value, does not prevent this transfer.
16	6. Dependencies of all still-usable places following the value remain valid; non-escape constraints and `AnchorOrder` are checked in the **resulting state**, including transferred anchors of owned places that remain usable.
17	7. All moved held authorities, including those of owned storage, satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state; no authority may escape a local anchor on the grounds that its containing value was transferred.
18	8. **Local self-blocking prevention:** For each active authority held before the step by a part `r` of `source` whose holder becomes the corresponding part `corr(r)` of `destination`, that authority's footprint contains **no leaf** of `corr(r)` in the resulting state. Transfer is rejected if this local check fails; no global authority-acyclicity check is imposed.
19	
20	**`ok` effect:**
21	
22	- every source leaf becomes `Moved` and each corresponding destination leaf becomes `Init`;
23	- every authority held by source part `r` acquires as its new holder the corresponding destination part `corr(r)`, not indiscriminately the destination root;
24	- places owned by `r` become owned by `corr(r)`; their roots follow this owner according to `RootHeld`;
25	- value dependencies follow the corresponding places under validity guarantees; no authority is created or duplicated;
26	- destination places receive the transferred values and rights without automatically moving storage not owned by a source part.
27	
28	**Other outcome:** `reject`. `transfer` to a call result is subject to these same rules.
29	
30	A partially initialized structure may be transferred **field by field**, but only for fields individually eligible for transfer. This does not automatically destructure a value that owns storage **at the container level**: that storage stays with the container if the container is not transferred. Conversion between structures with permuted fields must be handled separately, not as a `transfer`.
31	
32	## 64. O5 — Explicit Attachment of an Anchor
33	
34	**Preconditions**
35	
36	1. `result` is a usable place over which the current frame has exercisable `Modify`.
37	2. `anchor` designates an active, valid authority representing a real dependency of the relevant rights or storage; a declared dependency cannot extend an origin's lifetime.
38	3. Existing anchors are preserved and the addition respects `AnchorOrder`: the effective anchor's frame is the frame of `result` or an ancestor thereof.
39	4. Every dependency carried by a contained value remains represented in the transitive obligations of its container.
40	
41	**`ok` effect:** `anchor` is added to `D(result)`; the container's transitive dependencies account for it. No additional access right is created. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
42	
43	A safe interface must declare dependencies covering those actually required by its implementation; the annotation itself is not presumed true. An unsafe abstraction bears the obligations of its contract.
44	
45	## 65. O8 — Controlled Storage of an Authority
46	
47	**Preconditions**
48	
49	1. `authority` is active, **derived**, and held by the current frame; a root authority can never be stored by `store`.
50	2. `target` is a usable **leaf** under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It holds no other **active** authority. Its data already being `Init` does not by itself prohibit the operation.
51	3. The stored authority covers neither a leaf of `target` nor the leaves of storage transitively owned by it.
52	4. The effective anchor of `authority` respects `AnchorOrder` relative to the frame of `target`; other dependencies are preserved.
53	5. **In the resulting state**, `target` remains under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame (`store_keeps_target_reachable`), and `AnchorOrderHeld` remains true. This is a genuine additional precondition, not an automatic consequence of the preceding ones.
54	
55	**`ok` effect:** The holder of `authority` becomes `target`; the authority is added to `D(target)`; **only** leaf `target` becomes `Init`. Other fields of a structure, even adjacent ones, do not change their initialization state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
56	
57	Overwriting an active authority already held by the leaf is prohibited; its explicit release may make the target reusable. The resulting-state clause does not by itself prohibit all cycles possible after other operations: general freedom from blocking (`NoLock`) is not adopted here.
58	
59	# X. Reading, Writing, and Initialization
60	
61	A leaf's initialization state and the effective right to access it are two distinct conditions.
62	
63	## 66. O9 — Safe Reading of Regions
64	
65	**Preconditions**
66	
67	1. Every leaf being read belongs to a usable place and is `Init`.
68	2. `access` is an authority exercisable in `Observe` mode over the region; its **effective** mode actually permits observation of each leaf being read.
69	3. Required anchors are valid, and the type and storage contract permits this read.
70	
71	**`ok` effect:** The logical read succeeds, without modifying `F`, `P`, `I`, `A`, `D`, or arena entries. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
72	
73	`Moved` and `Uninit` cannot be read. This definition does not replace concrete representation and pointer checks of the elementary memory machine.
74	
75	## 67. O10 — Ordinary Write
76	
77	**Preconditions**
78	
79	1. Targeted leaves belong to usable places, and `access` is exercisable in `Modify` mode with **effective** `Modify` right over each leaf.
80	2. No incompatible ordinary authority holds an incompatible effective mode over the written leaves (I1).
81	3. Anchors and constraints of the relevant types, storage, and abstractions remain valid.
82	
83	**`ok` effect:** The logical write sets the actually written leaves to `Init` and does not modify authorities or their anchors. An unwritten leaf does not become `Init` by this effect. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
84	
85	## 68. O11 — Write Under Shared Mutation
86	
87	**Preconditions**
88	
89	1. Every leaf in the region is usable and declared `K.SharedMutable`.
90	2. `access` is exercisable in a mode **at least** `Observe` and has a present effective mode on every leaf, either `Observe` or `Modify`; exercising an authority without an effective mode is insufficient.
91	3. Dependencies are valid and the particular shared-mutation discipline guaranteed by `K.SharedMutable` applies.
92	
93	**`ok` effect:** Actually written leaves become `Init`; authorities and their structural exclusivity I1 do not change. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
94	
95	`writeShared` may update metadata under an `Observe` authority when the contract permits. Stability of observed contents is not automatically guaranteed, and this kernel **does not prove** the absence of data races: that requires the concurrency model's guarantees.
96	
97	# XI. End of Use, Deallocation, and Allocation
98	
99	The logical end of a value does not necessarily entail deallocation of its storage. The following operations treat initialization, ownership, and physical release separately.
100	
101	## 69. O12 — Logical End of a Value's Use
102	
103	**Preconditions**
104	
105	1. `place` is usable and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over it.
106	2. No active descendant over the leaves of `place` **or storage that dies with it** is held outside the places dying with `place`, in a way that would prevent rights from returning or being invalidated.
107	3. No place **remaining usable after the effect** depends on an authority held by `place`, its root, or an authority that would become inactive when an owned holder dies.
108	4. **No leaf whose use ends, including transitively owned storage, is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). A dynamic pinning obligation must be legally removed by `unpin` before this step.
109	
110	**`ok` effect:** The leaves of value `place` become `Uninit`; `place` **remains usable as a place** and may legally be reinitialized. Authorities held by `place` and dead substorages are released; dependencies of the ended value are removed; transitively owned places that cease to live are marked dead. The operation does not automatically trigger physical deallocation in the elementary memory machine: an unfreed allocation may constitute a leak, which this guarantee does not prohibit. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
111	
112	## 70. O13 — Release of an Owned Storage Unit
113	
114	**Preconditions**
115	
116	1. `place` is a **root of storage owned by a value** (`OwnedRoot`), not an ordinary local directly owned by a frame and not part of an aggregate.
117	2. `K.Deallocable(place)` is established, and `K.FreeCompat(place,auth)` justifies deallocation authority `auth`; this identifier is opaque to the authority kernel.
118	3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify`; no active derivative over the footprint being freed is held outside holders that die; no surviving place is anchored to an authority of the released region or of its dead holders.
119	4. No leaf of the released unit is statically or dynamically pinned. Ending external use does not silently turn a still-pinned leaf into a releasable unit.
120	
121	**`ok` effect:** `place` and the storage that ceases to live are marked dead; authorities of those regions, including their corresponding roots, become inactive, as do authorities whose holders die. Surviving dependencies must remain valid. Every realization of `free` must satisfy the corresponding deallocation relation of the elementary memory machine (Part III). **Other outcome:** `reject`.
122	
123	## 71. O14 — Allocation of a New Storage Root
124	
125	**Static preconditions**
126	
127	1. `shape` is a **nonempty** abstract shape, represented like the local places of `enterFrame`; an allocation of **zero physical size** may be represented by a logical one-leaf shape.
128	2. **All leaves of the provider** are `Init`; updates to its metadata are permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid `writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata.
129	3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify` over `owner`; new identities and ownership relations must respect `WF3`, `RootHeld`, and liveness restrictions.
130	
131	**Outcomes**
132	
133	- `reject`: a static precondition does not hold;
134	- `fail`: static preconditions hold, but `K.Satisfiable(provider,shape,s)` is false in the state under consideration; **no state change**;
135	- `ok(s')`: creation of a **new storage root** with fresh identity, owned by `owner`; its leaves start `Uninit`, its new root `Modify` authority with no origin is held by `owner`; provider metadata is updated only in accordance with its modification rights.
136	
137	Allocation success depends on the provider's state: it does not constitute a right to invent physical memory. Any realization of this operation must satisfy the `AllocStep` relation defined by the rules of Sections 9 and 13.
138	
139	# XII. Call Frames and Return of Authorities
140	
141	Frames are execution units that receive authorities, introduce locals, and have exit rules distinct from Spec 3's value-passing conventions.
142	
143	## 72. O6 — Entering a Frame
144	
145	**Preconditions**
146	
147	1. The calling frame is the current frame and is live. Each parameter passed to the callee is an active, derived authority held by the caller before the step; the caller is **not necessarily** the frame in which the authority was first derived.
148	2. Modes, footprints, anchoring, and parameter-passing rules permit this change of holder; introduction of locals preserves well-formedness and the validity of their roots.
149	3. **Origin protection on entry:** for each `Modify` parameter with direct origin `o`, `o` is exercisable in **no mode** (neither `Observe` nor `Modify`) in the **resulting state**, once the new frame's parameters and locals have been created.
150	4. **G4:** `AnchorOrderHeld` is checked over the complete resulting state.
151	
152	**`ok` effect:** A new child frame is pushed onto the stack; active parameters **are yielded** to that frame, which becomes their sole holder; local places and their root authorities are created; valid anchors inherited from the caller are preserved. This transfer creates no additional rights. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
153	
154	This clause establishes **entry protection**. It does not prove the stronger property of protection throughout the **entire** invocation following other releases or reanchorings. While a `Modify` parameter remains active, its direct origin remains subject to effective-mode restrictions. Any additional protection throughout the invocation is deferred to Spec 3.
155	
156	## 73. O7 — Exiting a Frame
157	
158	**Preconditions**
159	
160	1. The current frame is not the initial frame and has a surviving caller.
161	2. Results that must survive have already been legally transferred to their destinations; no active authority or dependency may remain invalidly attached to locals that are about to die.
162	3. **No leaf of a place that dies with the frame, including transitively owned storage, is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`).
163	4. Iterated reanchoring of surviving authorities and anchors reaches the **first surviving active origin**, held either by a surviving frame or by a usable place whose terminal owner survives; it is not permitted to skip a surviving origin merely because it is held by a place. The operation is rejected when no suitable surviving origin exists, particularly if the chain reaches a root of the exiting frame.
164	5. Validity of anchors of surviving values and `AnchorOrderHeld` are checked **in the resulting state**. Other state invariants and resource contracts are respected.
165	
166	**`ok` effect:**
167	
168	- the current frame is removed from the stack; its untransferred locals and substorages dying with them become unusable;
169	- authorities still held by that frame, or by places that have become unusable, are released;
170	- origins of surviving derived authorities are reanchored to the **first surviving active origin** of their chains, whether held by a frame or a usable place, and the `D` anchors of surviving values are correspondingly reanchored;
171	- reanchoring changes **neither the footprint nor the own mode** of an authority; parameter identities and relations specific to the frame cease their operational role;
172	- the calling frame becomes current again.
173	
174	**Other outcome:** `reject`. Exiting does not entail automatic physical deallocation of all dead places. Deferred cleanup (`defer`) lies outside this kernel. Reanchoring may change the current `origin` relation; protection of a historical borrow lineage during an invocation is a distinct, deferred question.
175	
176	# XIII. Pinning, Statics, and External Commitments
177	
178	Pinning forbids certain movements or ends of lifetime. It is not a general guarantee of content immutability.
179	
180	## 74. O15 — Dynamic Pinning
181	
182	**Preconditions:** `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over the relevant leaves, and the operation respects applicable pinning obligations.
183	
184	**`ok` effect:** A dynamic pinning obligation is installed on the relevant leaves. While it is active, `transfer`, `endUse`, `free`, and `exitFrame` are rejected if they act on leaves it pins; removal of this obligation requires `unpin` under `K.ExternalDone`. Pinning does not make contents immutable. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
185	
186	## 75. O16 — Removal of Dynamic Pinning
187	
188	**Preconditions:** `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify`, and contract `K.ExternalDone(place)` attests that all relevant external use has ended.
189	
190	**`ok` effect:** The corresponding dynamic pinning obligation ends, without itself modifying values, their initialization, or their access authorities. Static obligations are not removed by this operation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
191	
192	**Associated static rule (`StaticPinnedBottom`):** Statics designated by `K.Pinned` must be places **directly** owned by the **base frame**, not merely transitively owned by a static value. This restriction ensures that they do not die when an intermediate frame exits.
193	
194	# XIV. Arenas and Collective Invalidation — Reference Abstraction
195	
196	An arena is a **library abstraction**, not a memory-kernel primitive. Operations O17 through O19 are **derived** from operations O1 through O16 and abstraction-specific metadata: `newArena` registers an administration without modifying the kernel; `issue` performs `split` followed by `store` (after checking availability); `reset` performs a `Modify` derivation over all storage—through `derive` or `split`—then `release`, before restoring availability. Their contract below is **normative for the standard-library arena** until Spec 10 takes responsibility for it. It authorizes neither new permissions nor an additional access machine. Arena entries (Section 46) constitute the abstract state of this administration; the guard in Section 56 belongs to its consistency contract. The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here.
197	
198	## 76. O17 — Creation of an Administered Arena
199	
200	**Preconditions**
201	
202	1. `storage` is an existing, usable place under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame. It may be local, static, allocated, or a block issued by a previous arena.
203	2. `internal` is explicitly named by the caller, exists, is active, has own mode `Modify`, and `ExercisableAt(s,internal,Modify)` holds.
204	3. `internal` is **held by a place**: that place is the arena value; `footprint(internal) = footprint(storage)`.
205	4. **Unified administration guard (Section 56):** no **live** administrative abstraction, whether an arena or a library instance such as a handle pool, already uses this `internal` identity. The relevant registries of library administrations are consulted before registration. Two distinct identities may cover common leaves: this is not in itself grounds for rejection.
206	5. All leaves of the arena value holding `internal` are already `Init`; construction does not initialize them implicitly.
207	6. Dependency, holder, storage, and administration relations respect `WF3`, I1, `AnchorOrder`, `AnchorOrderHeld`, and the expected arena invariants.
208	
209	**`ok` effect:** A live entry `{storage, internal, available, issued}` is added; the initial `available` set represents the administered storage, and `issued` is initially empty. Registering the entry fabricates no place, access right, or `Init` state. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
210	
211	The identity of `internal`, not the index of `storage`, is the key to preventing duplication of live administrations. No global constraint requires footprints of live arenas to be pairwise disjoint.
212	
213	## 77. O18 — Issuing an Arena Block
214	
215	**Static preconditions**
216	
217	1. The `arena` entry exists and is live; `internal` is active. `MetaRight` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value holding `internal` (Section 36). Mutation of metadata through `writeShared` alone does not satisfy this condition.
218	2. `region` belongs to the administered storage; `destination` is a usable **leaf** holding no active authority; the destination can legally receive the block value in mode `Modify`. The fact that `destination` is already `Init` is not in itself grounds for rejection, in accordance with O8.2.
219	   **Local self-blocking prevention: leaf `destination` is not in `region`, including when the region is declared available.** This condition is static and is checked before an availability `fail`.
220	3. Applicable **static** validity and non-escape restrictions for the destination are satisfied. The `AnchorOrder` check depending on the new anchor is performed on the **simulated resulting state**, after the availability check described in point 4; it cannot turn an unavailable issuance (`fail`) into `reject`.
221	
222	**Availability and exercisability checks**
223	
224	4. If static conditions hold but **at least one leaf of `region` does not belong to `available`**, the operation produces **`fail` and leaves the entire state unchanged**. The empty region is always available. An unavailable region does not permit a prior static rejection to be bypassed.
225	5. If the region is available, the effective mode of `internal` on that region must permit `Modify`; otherwise the outcome is `reject`.
226	6. The simulated result must satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` **in the resulting state**; moreover, **in that resulting state, `destination` must remain under exercisable `Modify` by the current frame**, in accordance with O8.5. Issuance into a value with a longer lifetime than a local anchor is not made valid merely by storing it in the caller.
227	
228	**`ok` effect:** A block authority of fresh identity, derived from `internal` and of mode `Modify`, is issued for the region; it is held by `destination`, which receives the corresponding anchor. The leaves of the region leave `available`, and the issuance is added to `issued` with its authority. **Only leaf `destination` becomes `Init`**; no other leaf of the arena value changes initialization. Previous issuances remain intact and valid. Issuance does not automatically install anchors on third-party values: they must use their lawful dependency mechanisms.
229	
230	**Outcomes:** `ok`, `fail` (region unavailable after static validation), `reject` (static rule, effective right, or anchoring not satisfied). The destination may be a leaf of the arena value itself: its initialization then constitutes **an explicit write to that destination**, not implicit initialization of the entire arena value's metadata.
231	
232	## 78. O19 — Collective Arena Reset
233	
234	**Preconditions**
235	
236	1. The entry exists and is live. **`MetaRight(s,arena)` requires exercisable `Modify` over the arena value**, in accordance with Section 36. `writeShared` over metadata alone, even when legal, does not replace such exercise. `internal` and the arena's other restrictions remain valid.
237	2. **No active authority derived from `internal` covers a leaf of the administered storage.** A derived authority with an empty footprint does not, by itself, block `reset`.
238	3. No still-usable place depends, directly or transitively, on an anchor in the **strict origin subtree of `internal`** (`internal` itself is excluded). Under precondition 2 and invariant I3, this condition follows from the absence of active descendants covering the storage, and remains explicit in the abstraction contract. Validity obligations of other nested arenas remain satisfied.
239	
240	**`ok` effect:** All **leaves** of the administered storage become available again, and the issuance list is cleared under the arena contract. No still-active derived authority covering those leaves may remain, by precondition 2; an empty-footprint derivative may remain active without designating any recycled leaf. **No leaf is made `Init` by `reset`**, including in the arena value. **Other outcome:** `reject`.
241	
242	Safe reuse after `reset` requires that previous issuances **covering recycled leaves**, and the dependencies on which their validity rests, have effectively ceased preventing their reuse. Any active empty-footprint derivatives cover none of those leaves. A historically issued region does not remain permanently unavailable solely for that reason.
243	
244	# XV. Transitive Dependencies, Returns, and Value Behavior
245	
246	Dependent values may survive transfers and calls only if the required anchors and rights remain valid. Second-class access does not imply an arbitrary persistent reference.
247	
248	## 79. Non-Escaping Values and Returns
249	
250	The second-class nature of access authorities does not prohibit constructing a value carrying a derived authority or returning a result dependent on a caller-owned resource. What is prohibited is artificially extending the validity of a local origin.

250	The second-class nature of access authorities does not prohibit constructing a value carrying a derived authority or returning a result dependent on a caller-owned resource. What is prohibited is artificially extending the validity of a local origin.
251	
252	A typical scenario is:
253	
254	```text
255	arena = create_arena()
256	buffer = create_buffer(arena)
257	use(buffer)
258	endUse(buffer)       // or equivalent release of its dependent rights
259	arena.reset()
260	```
261	
262	The scenario is permitted when:
263	
264	1. the call receives and exercises valid authorities over the arena;
265	2. issuance supplies a block disjoint from live issuances;
266	3. the result value is anchored to the rights actually required;
267	4. its transfer to the caller respects `SameShape`, holders, `AnchorOrder`, and `AnchorOrderHeld`;
268	5. `exitFrame` can reanchor surviving authorities without using a dead local root;
269	6. `reset` is rejected while the dependent result or a block authority remains active, then becomes permitted after those rights have effectively ended.
270	
271	A “non-escaping” value is therefore not necessarily confined to the frame in which it was created. It may survive a function when it depends on a caller anchor, without extending dead local storage. This result does **not** imply strong protection of all parameter authorities throughout the entire invocation: the historical interpretation of reborrows and this property are deferred to Spec 3.
272	
273	Properties of transfer between threads and shareability do not follow from this sequential model alone. They depend on external resources, contained authorities, anchors, confinement restrictions, and the concurrency model of Spec 2.
274	
275	# XVI. External Contracts and Interfaces with Other Specifications
276	
277	Declarative contracts create no rights. Their satisfaction is an obligation of the language, typing, implementation, or a safe abstraction, according to the nature of each contract.
278	
279	## 80. Parametric Contracts of the Access Discipline
280	
281	A contract `K` parameterizes rules of the access discipline without fabricating permissions. A safe abstraction using part of `K` must prove or fulfill the corresponding obligation; an unestablished precondition is not a language guarantee.
282	
283	| Contract | External obligation |
284	|---|---|
285	| `DeclaredDisjoint` | `DDSound(K)`: no falsely declared disjoint region when leaves can overlap |
286	| `Pinned` | I5, prohibition of incompatible physical moves; `StaticPinnedBottom` for pinned statics |
287	| `SharedMutable` | Applicable shared-mutation discipline, with correct rights and synchronization |
288	| `ExternalDone` | External use of storage has ended when `unpin` is permitted |
289	| `Deallocable` | The place belongs to a unit that can actually be freed |
290	| `FreeCompat` | Opaque deallocation authority is compatible with the unit being freed |
291	| `Satisfiable` | The provider can satisfy the requested shape **in the current state** |
292	
293	Structural conditions of `free`, dependencies, and the derived library `reset` carry the relevant invalidation obligations. Physical justification of `DDSound` must be established by a realization consistent with memory layouts and Section 82.
294	
295	## 81. Boundaries Remaining to Be Specified
296	
297	This specification **does not by itself determine**: concurrency and synchronization effects (Spec 2); control-flow analysis, `defer`, and by-value calling conventions (Spec 3); representation criteria and typed formation of accesses (Spec 4); representation of library metadata, address width, encodings, and alignment/ABI obligations (Spec 11); or final translation of `noalias` properties (Spec 13). Leaving a rule open does not authorize a safe interface to cause UB; the implementation must fulfill or reject the obligations before exposing the operation to safe code.
298	
299	# XVII. Correspondence Between Access Discipline and Memory Machine
300	
301	A transition of the access discipline must admit a realization compatible with the bytes and allocations of the memory machine. An abstract definition of a right does not suffice to justify its concrete representation.
302	
303	## 82. Representation Relation and Concrete Obligations
304	
305	1. **Places and bytes:** relate `P`, `footprint` leaves, their ownership, and their parts to the storage units, offsets, ranges, identities, and alignment constraints of the elementary memory machine; establish actual disjointness for `DeclaredDisjoint` declarations.
306	2. **Authorities and operations:** connect effective modes and `ExercisableAt` to concrete read, write, and pointer-validity conditions; show that safe access governed by Parts VI through XV satisfies the obligations of Part III, without conflating ownership and binary representation.
307	3. **Initialization:** relate `Uninit`, `Init`, and `Moved` to concrete values and representations; an authority `store` must correspond to writing an actual reference into **a single logical leaf** with an appropriate representation.
308	4. **Allocation and deallocation:** relate `alloc` / `free` to `AllocStep` / `DeallocStep`, justify `Satisfiable`, `Deallocable`, and `FreeCompat`, as well as the zero-physical-size case.
309	5. **Lifetimes:** relate `endUse`, `exitFrame`, `NoDangling`, dependencies, and death markers to the validity effects on actual storage.
310	6. **Pinning and static storage:** prove compatibility of permitted moves and pinned-address restrictions; specify the physical obligations of statics and external use. Hardware-specific MMIO semantics remain outside the sequential kernel.
311	7. **Arenas:** show that the library abstraction's derived operations and metadata, distinct from `S₃`, can be realized by operations O1–O16; relate issued regions and local/static/allocated storage to the elementary memory machine without reintroducing access after invalidation.
312	8. **`noalias`:** infer no pointer-lowering property from abstract invariants alone; memory justification is established here and the translation choices at Spec 13 level.
313	
314	# XVIII. Examples of Semantic Behavior
315	
316	The fragments below are **traces of abstract operations**, not language syntax. The judgments illustrate normative rules; they create no exception to the detailed preconditions.
317	
318	## 83. Address Reuse and Old Provenance
319	
320	An allocation `a` is created and an access retains its provenance; after deallocation, a new allocation `b` may occupy the same address. `a ≠ b` as abstract identities: reading through the old access is invalid even if the addresses are equal. A new valid access with provenance `b` may be used within its rights.
321	
322	## 84. Partial Initialization and Reading
323	
324	A valid write to a subrange initializes its corresponding bytes. Reading another subrange that remains uninitialized is not permitted. The correspondence for logical state `Init` must guarantee a representation valid for the expected type; the mere presence of bits does not authorize type confusion.
325	
326	## 85. Splitting a Structure or SoA Columns
327	
328	Starting from a `Modify` authority exercised over a structure, `split` may provide `Modify` authorities over disjoint leaf regions. Modification of each region is permitted as long as the other validity and holder conditions hold; a second independent derivation over the same leaf does not become legal merely by having a distinct name.
329	
330	## 86. Arena, Active Views, and Reset
331	
332	Two disjoint issued regions may be used simultaneously with valid derived rights. `reset` is rejected while an issuance or active dependency would make recycling unsafe; after a legal end of use for all the relevant blocks, the region may be reissued. Reissuance does not permit reading a former logical value without the required initialization.
333	
334	## 87. Pinning an In-Place Value
335	
336	A pinned in-place leaf cannot be physically moved by `transfer`. If only an allocation owned by a value is pinned, transfer of that value may remain valid when the other conditions hold, because the owned allocation is not physically moved.
337	
338	## 88. Local Self-Blocking and Indirect Cycles
339	
340	An authority stored by `transfer` in a place that would then become its new holder cannot cover any leaf of that place. Likewise, `issue` cannot issue into a leaf belonging to the issued region, **or into a destination that would no longer be exercisable in `Modify` in the resulting state** (O8.5). These restrictions do not promise general freedom from authority cycles: indirect blocking compatible with safety may remain.
341	
342	## 89. Handles and Persistent References
343	
344	In a generation-based pool library abstraction, a handle may contain a logical pool identity, an entry identifier, and a generation. This handle is not, by itself, an access right. Safe resolution temporarily supplies authority when the pool and entry are valid; a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure. These conditions belong to the safe abstraction's contract and do not modify the authority-discipline kernel.
345	
346	## 90. Global and Called Frame
347	
348	Global storage is anchored to the base frame, but a called function does not acquire ambient authority to modify it merely by being invoked. To access a global, it receives a derived authority under `enterFrame` conditions and may exercise only its effective modes.
